critical_code_review_comments: operational_modes.migrate_default_modes uses `action` key in audit_log while some other subsystems use `event` — consider a single canonical field name across audit_log writers to simplify querying (my first-cut test failed until I discovered the inconsistency).

governance /propose endpoint accepts body {field, new_value} — no `from` snapshot in the request; server reads old_value from bot_configs. Correct defence but the frontend must render classification=aggressive even when old_value=null (as observed) — verify UX still communicates risk direction when the field was previously unset.

release-readiness returns HTTP 503 when overall ready=false (e.g., worker_leases FAIL in preview single-process mode) — this is correct fail-closed behaviour, but tests must accept 200 OR 503 and inspect checks.loop_progress independently. Documenting this behaviour in the API contract would help.

GovernanceCard testids: approve/reject use `governance-{action}-{id}` while confirm uses `governance-confirm-approve-{id}` — inconsistent naming (approve vs confirm-approve). Consider `governance-approve-confirm-{id}` for symmetry with `governance-approve-{id}`.
